newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia BoP deficit seen at $700 mln in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia BoP deficit seen at $700 mln in 1997.

text.p: Indonesia is expected to suffer a $700 million balance of payments (BoP) deficit in 1997, after enjoying a projected $200 million surplus this year, the Jakarta Post on Friday reported a domestic think tank as saying.

The paper quoted the Institute for Development of Economics and Finance as saying that net capital inflows, including official loans, were likely to reach $9.2 billion in 1997, up from expected $8.8 billion this year.
The capital inflows, however, would be too small to cover the country's current account deficit, the institute said.
It said Indonesia's current account deficit was projected to reach $9.9 billion next year, up from the $8.6 billion projected for this year.

"Next year could be critical year for us, and the government will do anything to cover the deficit. It may seek new loans, issue new bonds or use its stand-by loans," the paper quoted Faisal Basri, a researcher from institute, as saying.
The realisation of foreign direct investment commitments was expected to be weaker with many investors putting off their projects until after the 1997 general elections, Faisal said.
